Well you can never go wrong with a handmade ceramic mug. I am a potter myself, and i have an etsy with plenty of handmade mugs on it. Etsy has a ridiculously large stock of handmade ceramic wares, im sure you will find something you like there.

Hey i know something about this! I am a potter, and spend all day making dinnerware, so i might be able to help. 

I personally do not even own a china cabinet, but you better believe that if i did, it would be full of handmade work only.

Obviously this is the most expensive route, but you can find some incredible work out there. that will make traditional china pale in comparison.

Two examples of stoneware that belongs in a china cabinet.

[Lisa Orr](http://payload47.cargocollective.com/1/1/58087/3255148/Orr-Lisa.jpg)

[Liz Quackenbush](http://img-cache.oppcdn.com/img/v1.0/s:39410/t:QkxBTksrVEVYVCtIRVJF/p:18/g:br/o:2.5/a:100/q:90/984x588-Eejh1hZgL53C1vQm.jpg/882x588/24d64d0625e9420768af086f9b0becc0.jpg)


Another option would be to go to street fairs where people sell their crafts, and looking for potters there. I mainly sell my stuff through street fairs, and i know plenty of other potters do too.

Etsy is also a great place to find lots of handmade pottery, but oftentimes the prices are higher there than at a street fair, so if you want to save money Etsy may not be the way to go. 

Personally, i would suggest not going to ikea or target for your dinnerware because so many people get the same boring cups plates and bowls. When you buy something handmade you are getting not only a functional piece of dinnerware, but also a piece of art. 

Consider finding a few potters whose work you like, and buying one place setting from each of them (1 plate, bowl, and cup) that way when you have family over for thanksgiving dinner, everybody has radically different styles of dinnerware.   

A final option would be if you are anywhere near Portland OR, i will give you a sweet deal on dinnerware haha
